65446103.extract:
## Appearances

### Mario Kart series

Cows debuted in Mario Kart 64 on the Moo Moo Farm course, where they appear as stationary background animals in the pastures. In Mario Kart: Double Dash!! (2003), they are referenced indirectly through an advertisement on a truck in the Mushroom City course, promoting Moo Moo Farm.

In Mario Kart DS (2005), cows return on the retro version of Moo Moo Farm, now depicted with blue collars and golden bells. They serve as background elements but do not interact with gameplay.

Mario Kart Wii (2008) features cows as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows, where colliding with them causes racers to spin out. Distant cows use simplified textures, while closer ones have detailed models. An advertisement for Moo Moo Dairy appears on a truck in the Moonview Highway course.

In Mario Kart 7 (2011), cows are shown on a Moo Moo Dairy sign in the retro Wii Coconut Mall course, but they do not appear physically.

Mario Kart 8 (2014) and its enhanced version, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe (2017), include cows as obstacles on the retro Wii Moo Moo Meadows, with variations in color: white with blue or brown spots, black, or brown. Advertisements for Moo Moo Meadows Milk appear in courses like Toad Harbor and Toad's Turnpike. A Mii Racing Suit based on a cow design is available in Mario Kart 8 Deluxe.

In Mario Kart Tour (2019), cows do not appear directly, but Moo Moo Meadows Milk is a sponsor, and items include the Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit and Moo Moo Offroader vehicle.

Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit (2020) uses cows as obstacles in the Windmill Meadows course.

In Mario Kart World (2025), cows return as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows. Additionally, a single cow is a playable character, classified as a heavyweight racer with statistics including speed of 60, acceleration of 45, weight of 55, and handling of 40. The character is available from the start and shares its weight class with characters such as Wario and Donkey Kong. Gameplay includes missions like navigating through a herd of cows within 15 seconds. A golden cow statue on a bike appears in the game.

### Other games

In Mario Party 2 (2000), cows appear as background elements in the Western Land board.

Mario Party 3 (2001) features cows in the background of the Fowl Play minigame.

In Mario Pinball Land (2004), cows rarely emerge from holes after hitting a Monty Mole; striking one grants 100,000 points.

Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (2012) includes cows as obstacles in the Dream Equestrian event, set on Moo Moo Meadows.

In Mario Party: Island Tour (2013), cows are background elements on the Perilous Palace Path board.

Yoshi's Woolly World (2015) and its port Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World (2017) feature a Moo Moo Yoshi pattern that players can unlock.

In Yoshi's Crafted World (2019), Moo Moo Meadows Milk appears as a sponsor on cartons and signs in the Rail-Yard Run and Go-Go Yoshi levels. Players collect five cardboard cow crafts as souvenirs and can equip Yoshi with a cow costume.

Super Mario Party Jamboree (2024) includes cows in the Western Land area.

In the Super Mario Mash-Up Pack for Minecraft (2016), the cow design replaces the standard cow mob, with red and green variants substituting for Mooshrooms.

Nintendo Badge Arcade (2014) offers collectible badges featuring cows from the Mario Kart 8 set.

## Design and characteristics

Cows in the Mario franchise are depicted as white animals with black spots, small horns, and beady eyes. From Mario Kart DS onward, they wear blue collars with golden bells. In Mario Kart 8 and later titles, they appear in multiple colors, including black and brown. The playable cow in Mario Kart World resembles the species but includes distinctive features such as a nose ring and a stylized face emblem. It poses on all fours during jumps to reflect its animal nature and drives vehicles in an upright position during races.

## Development

The inclusion of a playable cow in Mario Kart World stemmed from a designer's sketch during early development of a ranch-themed course. Producer Masaaki Ishikawa described the moment as pivotal, stating that the idea felt natural and led to incorporating other obstacle elements, such as Cheep Cheep and Pokey, as racers. These characters are categorized as "NPC Racers" to create a sense of an interconnected game world. Development involved challenges in animating and voicing the cow to align with established characters, including quadrupedal posing for authenticity. The concept also inspired the Kamek item, which transforms racers into NPC forms mid-race.

Mario Kart World was released on June 5, 2025, alongside the Nintendo Switch 2 console.

| **First appearance** | _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_64 "Mario Kart 64")_ ([1996](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#1996 "List of games by date")) |
| **Latest appearance** | _[Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super\_Mario\_Party\_Jamboree\_%E2%80%93\_Nintendo\_Switch\_2\_Edition\_%2B\_Jamboree\_TV "Super Mario Party Jamboree – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Jamboree TV")_ ([2025](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_games_by_date#2025 "List of games by date")) |

**Cows** (also referred to as **Moo Moos**)[[1]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[[2]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) appear as a recurring species in the [_Super Mario_ franchise](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super_Mario_(franchise) "Super Mario (franchise)"), first appearing in _[Mario Kart 64](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_64 "Mario Kart 64")_. They are primarily associated with farm-based courses in the _[Mario Kart](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart "Mario Kart")_ series, in which they typically act as obstacles.

- [x]

History[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### _Mario Kart_ series[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Mario Kart series")]

#### _Mario Kart 64_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Mario Kart 64")]

[![Image 51: Moo Moo Farm from Mario Kart 64.](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/e/e3/Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png/200px-Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png)

[](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Moo_Moo_Farm_MK64.png "Enlarge")

_Mario Kart 64_

Cows can be seen in the background of the _Mario Kart 64_ course [Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm").

#### _Mario Kart: Double Dash!!_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")]

Although cows themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart: Double Dash!!](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart:\_Double\_Dash!! "Mario Kart: Double Dash!!")_, [Mushroom City](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mushroom_City "Mushroom City") has a truck advertising the Moo Moo Farm course with the image of a cow.

#### _Mario Kart DS_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Mario Kart DS")]

In _[Mario Kart DS](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_DS "Mario Kart DS")_, cows once again appear in the background of [N64 Moo Moo Farm](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Farm "Moo Moo Farm"). It is the first game to give them the blue collars with hanging golden bells.

#### _Mario Kart Wii_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mario Kart Wii")]

[![Image 52: A cow in MKW](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/6/60/MushroomCow.png/140px-MushroomCow.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MushroomCow.png)

[](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MushroomCow.png "Enlarge")

A Moo Moo as seen in _Mario Kart Wii_

In _[Mario Kart Wii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_Wii "Mario Kart Wii")_, cows serve as obstacles in the course [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows"). When hit, they cause the player to spin out. While the ones seen up close use full models, some in the distant background reuse flat textures from _Mario Kart DS_. A truck in the [Moonview Highway](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moonview_Highway "Moonview Highway") course also has a picture of a cow printed on it with the text "[Moo Moo Dairy](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_Wii#Moo_Moo_Dairy "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart Wii")".

#### _Mario Kart 7_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Mario Kart 7")]

Two cows make a small appearance in _[Mario Kart 7](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_7 "Mario Kart 7")_ on a sign in the [Wii Coconut Mall](https://www.mariowiki.com/Coconut_Mall "Coconut Mall") course, which reads "Moo Moo Dairy".

#### _Mario Kart 8_ / _Mario Kart 8 Deluxe_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Mario Kart 8 / Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")]

Moo Moos return in _[Mario Kart 8](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_8 "Mario Kart 8")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_8\_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ with the return of the Moo Moo Meadows track, with some Moo Moos now having other colors, such as solid black or brown. Also, in [Toad Harbor](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad_Harbor "Toad Harbor") and the game's rendition of [Toad's Turnpike](https://www.mariowiki.com/Toad%27s_Turnpike "Toad's Turnpike"), there are advertising trucks and signs with Moo Moos on them. There is also a sponsor known as [Moo Moo Meadows Milk](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_brands_debuting_in_Mario_Kart_8_and_Mario_Kart_8_Deluxe#Moo_Moo_Meadows_Milk "List of brands debuting in Mario Kart 8 and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe"). In this game, Moo Moos appear in four different colors; white with blue spots, white with brown spots, black, or brown. The Mii Racing Suit based on a Moo Moo appears in the _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_8\_Deluxe\_%E2%80%93\_Booster\_Course\_Pass "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe – Booster Course Pass")_.

#### _Mario Kart Tour_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Mario Kart Tour")]

[![Image 53: The Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit from Mario Kart Tour](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/c/c0/MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png/60px-MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png)

[](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKT_Artwork_MooMooMiiRacingSuit.png "Enlarge")

Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor returns in several courses in the game, and the [Moo Moo Mii Racing Suit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") and [Moo Moo Offroader](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Offroader "Moo Moo Offroader") are both based on them and were introduced in the [Animal Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Animal_Tour "Animal Tour").

#### _Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")]

In _[Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_Live:\_Home\_Circuit "Mario Kart Live: Home Circuit")_, the [Windmill Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Windmill_Meadows "Windmill Meadows") features some Moo Moos as obstacles.

#### _Mario Kart World_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Mario Kart World")]

[![Image 54: Cow in Mario Kart World](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/3/37/MKWMooMoo.jpg/200px-MKWMooMoo.jpg)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWMooMoo.jpg)

[](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:MKWMooMoo.jpg "Enlarge")

Cow racing in _Mario Kart World_.

In _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_World "Mario Kart World")_, cows return as obstacles on Moo Moo Meadows. In addition, a cow appears as a playable character for the first time in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super\_Mario\_(franchise) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ franchise as a whole. Her [emblem](https://www.mariowiki.com/Emblem "Emblem") consists of a stylized depiction of her face. Moo Moo Meadows also now features a large golden statue of a cow on a bike.

The playable cow is unlockable in version 1.0.0, but made available from the start following a software update. She is a heavyweight character, sharing statistics with [Wario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wario "Wario"), [Waluigi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Waluigi "Waluigi"), [Donkey Kong](https://www.mariowiki.com/Donkey_Kong "Donkey Kong"), [Wiggler](https://www.mariowiki.com/Wiggler "Wiggler"), [Chargin' Chuck](https://www.mariowiki.com/Chargin%27_Chuck "Chargin' Chuck"), and [Pianta](https://www.mariowiki.com/Pianta "Pianta").

Missions
Cows are featured in the following [missions](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Mario_Kart_World_missions "List of Mario Kart World missions") in _Mario Kart World_:

| Mission | Location | Time limit (seconds) | Description |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| [![Image 55: Mario Kart World P-Switch Mission "Moove through the herd of cows!"](https://mario.wiki.gallery/images/thumb/f/f8/Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png/200px-Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png)](https://www.mariowiki.com/File:Mario_Kart_World_P_Switch_Missions_Moove.png) _Mooove through the herd of cows!_ | [Moo Moo Meadows](https://www.mariowiki.com/Moo_Moo_Meadows "Moo Moo Meadows") | 15.00 | The player must maneuver through a large crowd of cows and reach the goal ring in time. |

### _Mario Party_ series[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Mario Party series")]

Moo Moos make four background appearances in the [_Mario Party_ series](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario_Party_(series) "Mario Party (series)"). They appear in the background of [Western Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Western_Land "Western Land") in _[Mario Party 2](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Party\_2 "Mario Party 2")_ and _[Super Mario Party Jamboree](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super\_Mario\_Party\_Jamboree "Super Mario Party Jamboree")_ and [Fowl Play](https://www.mariowiki.com/Fowl_Play "Fowl Play") in _[Mario Party 3](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Party\_3 "Mario Party 3")_, and in _[Mario Party: Island Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Party:\_Island\_Tour "Mario Party: Island Tour")_, they appear on [Perilous Palace Path](https://www.mariowiki.com/Perilous_Palace_Path "Perilous Palace Path").

### _Mario Pinball Land_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Mario Pinball Land")]

In _[Mario Pinball Land](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Pinball\_Land "Mario Pinball Land")_, there is a rare chance for a Moo Moo to pop out of a hole by hitting a [Monty Mole](https://www.mariowiki.com/Monty_Mole "Monty Mole"). If [Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario "Mario") hits the Moo Moo before it disappears, he gains 100,000 [points](https://www.mariowiki.com/Point "Point").

### _Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games")]

Cows reappear in _[Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_%26\_Sonic\_at\_the\_London\_2012\_Olympic\_Games\_(Wii) "Mario & Sonic at the London 2012 Olympic Games (Wii)")_ on Moo Moo Meadows as obstacles in the [Dream Equestrian](https://www.mariowiki.com/Dream_Equestrian "Dream Equestrian") event.

### _Yoshi_ series[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Yoshi series")]

#### _Yoshi's Woolly World_ / _Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Yoshi's Woolly World / Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")]

Although Moo Moos themselves do not appear in _[Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s\_Woolly\_World "Yoshi's Woolly World")_ and _[Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Poochy\_%26\_Yoshi%27s\_Woolly\_World "Poochy & Yoshi's Woolly World")_, Moo Moo Yoshi is available as an unlockable Yoshi [pattern](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_Yoshi_designs_in_Yoshi%27s_Woolly_World "List of Yoshi designs in Yoshi's Woolly World") which resembles a Moo Moo.

#### _Yoshi's Crafted World_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Yoshi's Crafted World")]

In _[Yoshi's Crafted World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Yoshi%27s\_Crafted\_World "Yoshi's Crafted World")_, the Moo Moo Meadows Milk sponsor from _Mario Kart 8_ makes various cameo appearances on the cartons and signs in the background of the flip side of [Rail-Yard Run](https://www.mariowiki.com/Rail-Yard_Run "Rail-Yard Run") and [Go-Go Yoshi](https://www.mariowiki.com/Go-Go_Yoshi "Go-Go Yoshi"). As first seen on the front side of Rail-Yard Run, there are also five cardboard Cow [crafts](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_crafts_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of crafts in Yoshi's Crafted World"), which serve as [Coal Blockafeller](https://www.mariowiki.com/Blockafeller "Blockafeller")'s first souvenir request. There is additionally a Cow [costume](https://www.mariowiki.com/List_of_costumes_in_Yoshi%27s_Crafted_World "List of costumes in Yoshi's Crafted World") for Yoshi to wear.

### Other appearances[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Other appearances")]

#### _Nintendo Badge Arcade_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Nintendo Badge Arcade")]

Cows[[3]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) appear as badges in _[Nintendo Badge Arcade](https://www.mariowiki.com/Nintendo\_Badge\_Arcade "Nintendo Badge Arcade")_ that the player may collect and decorate their Nintendo 3DS HOME Menu with. They are a part of the _Mario Kart 8_ set of badges.

#### _Minecraft_[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Minecraft")]

In the Super Mario Mash-Up Pack in _[Minecraft](https://www.mariowiki.com/Minecraft "Minecraft")_, the traditional [Cow](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Cow "minecraftwiki:Cow")'s design is replaced with the Moo Moo design found in the _[Super Mario](https://www.mariowiki.com/Super\_Mario\_(franchise) "Super Mario (franchise)")_ titles. Red and green Moo Moos with mushrooms on their back replace Mooshrooms.

Naming[[edit](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow?action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Naming")]
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The name "Cow" (capitalized as such) is used in-game in _[Mario Kart World](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_World "Mario Kart World")_. Prior to this, supplementary material variously referred to them as "cows" (in lowercase)[[4]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4)[[5]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-7)[[3]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-badge-3) or "Moo Moos"[[1]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMoo-1)[[2]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-MooMooTwo-2) (alternatively lowercased as "moo moos"),[[4]](https://www.mariowiki.com/Cow#cite_note-switch-4) with the latter being primarily used by third-party guidebooks. Though the name "Moo Moo" has never been explicitly used to refer to them in-game, it is implied in _[Mario Kart Tour](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_Tour "Mario Kart Tour")_ and _[Mario Kart 8 Deluxe](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mario\_Kart\_8\_Deluxe "Mario Kart 8 Deluxe")_ by the name of the Moo Moo [Mii](https://www.mariowiki.com/Mii "Mii") Racing Suit.

["This Is It!" - Nintendo On Why It Added 'Cow' Into Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/news/2025/05/this-is-it-nintendo-on-why-it-added-cow-into-mario-kart-world)
===============================================================================================================================================================================

What an udder surprise

[![Image 30: MK World - Cow 2](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.900x.jpg)](https://images.nintendolife.com/5686ba9dfd94f/mk-world-cow-2.large.jpg "MK World - Cow 2")

_Image: Nintendo_

If you watched any of the reactions to the [Mario Kart World](https://www.nintendolife.com/games/nintendo-switch-2/mario-kart-world) reveal trailer, then chances are you saw somebody loudly exclaim "you can play as a _COW?!"_.

Yes, the cow, an NPC character known for its presence in Moo Moo Meadows, is now playable in the upcoming Mario Kart tile for Switch 2. In the recent [Ask the Developer](https://www.nintendo.com/us/whatsnew/ask-the-developer-vol-18-mario-kart-world-part-3/) interview over at Nintendo, Masaaki Ishikawa explained the reasoning behind Cow's inclusion.

Honestly, it seems to have simply been a case of pondering what new additions could be added after Mario Kart 8 Deluxe included so many newcomers. Here's what Ishikawa had to say:

> "Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that's when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> 
> "The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn't feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world."

Characters such as Cow and Cheep Cheep are known as 'NPC Racers' within Nintendo, with Ishikawa joking that Cow in particular "is actually a pivotal character in the Mario Kart series".

To coincide with the information from the Ask the Developer interview, Nintendo has also released new footage from Mario Kart World showcasing Cow taking part in one of the game's missions, as shown by [TodayNews on BlueSky.](https://bsky.app/profile/today.oatmealdome.me/post/3lpousecsiy2c) The task? "Mooove" through a herd of cows, of course. Chortle!

Mario Kart World is scheduled to launch alongside the Switch 2 on **5th June 2025**. Nintendo also revealed that the game was originally in development for Switch 1, and also explained why it chose not to call the game 'Mario Kart 9'.

Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World

Nintendo Explains How The Cow Became A Playable Character In Mario Kart World
=============================================================================

##### [7 months ago](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/ "7 months ago") [Iggy](https://nintendosoup.com/author/iggynosuupu/ "View all posts by Iggy") Comments [0 Comment](https://nintendosoup.com/nintendo-explains-how-the-cow-became-a-playable-character-in-mario-kart-world/#respond)

In the first developer interview for Mario Kart World, Nintendo developers shared how the Cow became a playable character in Mario Kart World.

When working on an early version of a course in the game, a sketch of a cow driving a kart came up. This led to character designer quickly putting together a prototype of Cow that could race, which didn’t feel out of place. Nintendo then later expanded the idea to other obstacle characters, such as Cheep Cheep and Pokey. Thanks to the addition of the obstacle drivers, the Kamek item was born, and more obstacle characters were turned into drivers as a result:

> **Now that you mention it, some of the new characters in this game seem like unlikely picks. I was surprised to see Cow as one of the playable characters.**
> 
> **Yabuki**: That’s right. In previous games in the series, Cow was part of the scenery or an obstacle on one of the courses. But when we were working on an early version of a course in this game set on a ranch that players can drive through, this sketch came up. (Laughs)
> 
> **Oh, I thought Cow was just on the back of the truck, but she’s actually driving it. (Laughs)**
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Each new _Mario Kart_ game features new characters to race with, but since we added so many to the previous game, we wondered where we could go from there. And then one of the designers came up with that silly sketch of Cow cruising along, and I thought to myself, “This is it!” (Laughs) So that’s when we realized the course surroundings actually contained a lot of untapped resources.
> 
> The character designer quickly put together a prototype of Cow that could race, and surprisingly it didn’t feel out of place at all. So we thought maybe we could include other obstacle characters, and decided to add Cheep Cheep and Pokey as racers. As a result, the idea of taking obstacle characters, usually found in courses in past games, and having them participate in races made sense to me in terms of an interconnected world.
> 
> **Sato**: We called these types of characters “NPC drivers.” In other words, non-player character drivers.
> 
> **Yabuki**: So it was like, “They’re NPCs, but they’re playable? Which is it?” (Laughs) It’s pretty funny to see a four-legged Cow holding onto motorcycle handlebars with her front hooves.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: But when she jumps, she strikes a proper quadrupedal pose. So I’m pretty sure Cow is still in touch with her animal nature. (Laughs)
> 
> **Jikumaru**: It was thanks to the introduction of various “NPC drivers” that the idea to have Kamek appear as an item was born. When Kamek casts a spell, the racers are transformed into playable NPCs, so one by one they might all turn into Cow mid-race. I think it turned out to be a unique item that has never been seen before. In fact, Cow is a character who’s inspired a lot of different ideas, including obstacle characters like Camel and Giraffe.
> 
> **Ishikawa**: Cow is actually a pivotal character in the _Mario Kart_ series. (Laughs)
> 
> **Asahi**: On the other hand, when previously non-playable characters like Cow become playable, it means giving them new ways to express emotion, which must have been difficult for the voice lead. We were conscious of depicting the personalities and characteristics of “NPC drivers” in a way that doesn’t look inferior to classic characters like Mario. The voice team members went through a lot of trial and error in the pursuit of the ideal sound. In addition to more characters, this game also has a wider selection of vehicles for characters to drive, so it was a huge task to create engine sounds that matched the characteristics, such as the appearance and structure, of each vehicle. We tried out a lot of different sounds in our search for something ideal—we even used croaking frogs and beating drums. (Laughs)
> 
> **Sato**: There are a lot of vehicles in this game, too. Since the game is about racing around the world, we’ve included not only race karts, but also everyday vehicles. It must have been tough for the designers, as they had to not only design the body of the vehicle, but also consider how the tires would transform when drifting and how the vehicle would move when jumping.

What do you think? Let us know in the comments.

11.title: 'Mario Kart World' release: Where to buy, new features and more
11.description: Wahoo! It’s time for the release of 'Mario Kart World.' Are you ready to play?
11.content:
_Mario Kart World_, the ninth edition of [Nintendo](https://tech.yahoo.com/gaming/nintendo/)'s beloved racing game, comes out today. And while fans of the games (and perhaps the movie, and the Universal theme park rides) can expect to see a lot of familiar Mario Kart elements, there's also plenty of new stuff to look forward to — and a whole new Nintendo device to secure so you can play. Here’s everything you need to know before playing _Mario Kart World_, including where you can pre-order the game, how to get the [Nintendo Switch 2](https://www.engadget.com/gaming/nintendo/nintendo-switch-2-pre-order-updates-the-latest-on-restocks-my-nintendo-store-invites-and-more-140931152.html), new game modes, confirmed courses and more.

**_Mario Kart World_****release date:**
---------------------------------------

_Mario Kart World_ comes out on June 5 in conjunction with the Nintendo Switch 2. [Pre-orders are open now](https://shopping.yahoo.com/rdlw?merchantId=3719d8d4-5edd-4817-998a-91f3229e7323&itemId=walmart_transaction_15940407280&siteId=us-tech&pageId=1p-autolink&contentUuid=b07b3011-22df-4e58-9c9e-db32a473109a&featureId=text-link&merchantName=Walmart&linkText=Pre-orders+are+open+now&&signature=AQAAAZ119ixA3lxTtbbsQHce1IDoCy8uXjC47ovbKX6197TD&gcReferrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.walmart.com%2Fip%2FMario-Kart-World-U-S-Version%2F15940407280%3F&spaceId=1197810144&uuid=YzzqFZl7LO1Yp54P30237) for the new game.

**_Mario Kart World_****modes:**
--------------------------------

The new Mario Kart game features two flagship modes: Grand Prix mode, which consists of a series of four races in pursuit of the podium and a Cup (of which there are seven), and Knockout Tour mode, where you race in elimination-style matches.

There are also Time Trials, Vs. Race, Battle Mode and Free Roam, which allows you to drive around and explore the whole of _Mario Kart World._

There's rumor of a Reverse mode after characters were spotted racing in reverse in a Japan-only _Mario Kart World_ ad. Perhaps an unlockable mode to replace Mirror mode? Time will tell if that rumor proves true.

### Mario Kart World gameplay

![Image 49: New Mario Kart screenshot](https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fbDLWy2tGEQtQhRHocj7of.jpg)

(Image credit: Nintendo)

_Mario Kart World_ gameplay was shown off during the Nintendo Switch 2 reveal event that aired on April 2, 2025. In it, we see that all tracks in the game lead into one another, in a large interconnected world map. This allows players to drive between tracks during Grand Prix. In addition, you can drive anywhere on a track, even outside of the guidelines. There's another mode called Knockout Tour, which takes you from one end of the world to the other. Speed towards checkpoints, as the players in last place are eliminated.

From what we've seen so far, _Mario Kart World_ features a bunch of new mechanics. The first is the ability to grind, which is shown in the reveal trailer. Players can seemingly drive into larger vehicles and take them over as well. There are new items to play with too, like a burger seen in the aforementioned trailer. There's wall-riding, and an expanded flying mechanic as well. New tricks and items are now available too, with Charge Jump being handy for dodging items and other hazards.

Races can now contain 24 players, the largest in the series so far. This all pairs nicely with the new Free Roam mode that lets you and your friends drive around the map, completing challenges. New items include Coin Shell, which spawns a line of coins to collect. Hammer can be thrown at enemies in an arc. Mega Mushroom makes you grow massively in size, and Kamek casts spells that affect other players.

[](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/mario-kart-world-release-date)
Is Mario Kart World Nintendo Switch 2 only?
-------------------------------------------

Yes, _Mario Kart World_ is being developed exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. It will not be available on the previous console.

[](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/mario-kart-world-release-date)
Does Mario Kart World have splitscreen?
---------------------------------------

_Mario Kart World_ does indeed have splitscreen. You can also play online, though a Nintendo Online subscription is required.

[](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/mario-kart-world-release-date)
### Mario Kart World news

**Nintendo confirms the Nintendo Switch 2 Joy-Con controllers have been 'designed from the ground up' and I couldn't be happier**Nintendo has confirmed that [the Nintendo Switch 2 Joy-Con 2 controllers have been redesigned](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/nintendo-confirms-the-nintendo-switch-2-joy-con-controllers-have-been-designed-from-the-ground-up-and-i-couldnt-be-happier), hopefully, to avoid potential stick drift.

During an [exclusive hands-on preview of the Nintendo Switch 2](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/nintendo-switch-2-hands-on-preview), TechRadar Gaming asked Technology Development Division general manager Tetsuya Sasaki if any improvements have been made to prevent Joy-Con stick drift.

Sasaki responded, confirming that the new magnetic Joy-Con 2 controllers have been completely redesigned for smoother gameplay.

**Mario Kart World has been revealed**

[Mario Kart World has now been officially revealed](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/mario-kart-world-officially-revealed-as-a-nintendo-switch-2-exclusive), and it's a launch title!

**Mario Kart World teased**

What we now know to be _Mario Kart World_ was [first teased during the first look at Nintendo Switch 2 event](https://www.techradar.com/gaming/i-just-watched-the-nintendo-switch-2-trailer-and-hold-on-is-that-a-new-mario-kart). We only saw a brief glimpse of gameplay, but it certainly got the internet talking.

**_Mario Kart World_ is set to release alongside the Switch 2 on Thursday, June 5, 2025**. Gamers who have ordered a physical version of _Mario Kart World_ or plan to purchase it in stores will be able to play it as soon as their local retailers add it to their stock this Thursday.

Players who get the Switch 2 bundle with [_Mario Kart World_](https://gamerant.com/db/video-game/mario-kart-world/) as a digital download code or get it separately in the eShop will be able to play at midnight in most regions. However, in regions where there are several time zones, it can be a bit more complicated. **In the US, Nintendo games tend to release at 9 PM PT on the night before it's official launch date, which coincides with midnight in the eastern timezone**, **but this is an exception, and in other regions, gamers will have to wait for 12 AM local time.**

Even though release times for Switch 2 games have not been disclosed yet, there is no reason to believe that they will be any different compared to the original Switch model.[According to the official Nintendo of America website](https://en-americas-support.nintendo.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/17395/~/when-are-new-games-added-to-the-nintendo-eshop%3F), digital software that is also sold physically becomes available at 9 PM PT the day before its physical launch.
